title: the gaps programme at tng lxxxii. the first atmospheric investigation of the gas giant wasp-13b at high resolution with giarps
abstract: low-density transiting gas giant exoplanets are key benchmarks for atmospheric studies. despite their large-scale heights, many of them remain poorly characterised. we present the first atmospheric investigation at high-resolution of the inflated (r$_\mathrm{p}$$\sim$1.4 r$_{\mathrm{j}}$), hot jupiter (t$\sim$1500$ \mathrm{k}$) wasp-13 b aiming at constraining its atmospheric composition and refine its orbital geometry. we analysed four transits observed with giarps at the tng. updated stellar and planetary parameters were re-derived from the most precise literature values, and a new rossiter-mclaughlin analysis was performed to measure the projected spin-orbit angle ($λ$) and stellar rotational velocity ($v\sin{i_\star}$). atmospheric signals were searched using high-resolution spectroscopy, both with cross-correlation and single-line analyses, targeting key atomic and molecular species (e.g. \ion{he}{i}, h$α$, \ion{na}{i}, h$_2$o, co). we find a well-aligned orbit ($λ$ = 2.7$\pm$1.1$^\circ$) and $v\sin{i_\star}$ = 4.5$\pm$0.1 km s$^{-1}$, improving upon previous constraints. no significant atmospheric absorption is detected in either vis or nir data. injection-and-recovery tests exclude an isothermal atmosphere with metallicity [m/h]$\lesssim$10$\times$[m/h]$_\odot$ and simultaneously a grey cloud top pressure p$_{\rm cloud}\gtrsim10$ mbar, under the assumption of chemical equilibrium. wasp-13 b appears to belong to the class of low-density hot jupiters with weak or featureless transmission spectra, most likely shaped by the presence of high-altitude clouds. although a highly metal-enriched atmosphere cannot be fully excluded, current evidence disfavours this scenario. further observations with next-generation facilities will be essential to characterise the atmospheric properties of this challenging target.
